summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypertension, aortic stenosis, chronic bronchitis, anemia, and recent pneumonia was admitted for evaluation of shortness of breath and abnormal EKG findings from his primary care visit. He denied chest pain but had mild anterior chest discomfort and chronic dyspnea unchanged from baseline. Cardiac enzymes were repeatedly normal, telemetry showed no arrhythmias, and chest imaging revealed no acute process, effectively ruling out myocardial infarction. His hypertension was managed with the addition of amlodipine due to persistently elevated blood pressure. Anemia and hyponatremia remained stable and were not actively treated. The patient's symptoms were attributed to resolving pneumonia and chronic lung disease. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and plans for outpatient follow-up and respiratory therapy evaluation.
